This vignette walks through an end-to-end epidemiological analysis workflow with
`OverReact`: cleaning survey inputs, inspecting missingness, describing the study
population (`tableOne()` and `tableOneDisplay()`), estimating unstratified and
stratified prevalence (`makeTablesNew()` and `stratifiedTables()`), fitting
sequentially adjusted regression models across multiple families including Cox
proportional-hazards models (`ModelMakerMultiRD()`), formatting regression tables
for publication (`modelOutputDisplay()`), plotting forest and VIF diagnostics
(`plotReactForest()` and `plotReactVIF()`), generating automated reports
(`run_auto_tableone_regressions()`), and exporting outputs.

```{r setup}
library(OverReact)
library(ggplot2)
set.seed(123)
```

## 1. Simulated study dataset

We simulate a cohort of $n = 800$ participants with demographic covariates, a continuous
primary exposure, binary and continuous outcomes, count outcomes with follow-up time, an
ordinal severity outcome, right-censored survival times, and dirty survey-coded fields.

```{r data}
n <- 800
dat <- data.frame(
  age_years = round(rnorm(n, mean = 50, sd = 15)),
  sex = factor(sample(c("Female", "Male"), n, replace = TRUE)),
  region = factor(
    sample(c("North", "Midlands", "South"), n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.30, 0.30, 0.40)),
    levels = c("South", "Midlands", "North")
  ),
  deprivation = factor(
    sample(paste0("Q", 1:5), n, replace = TRUE),
    levels = paste0("Q", 1:5)
  ),
  smoking_status = factor(
    sample(c("Never", "Former", "Current"), n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.55, 0.25, 0.20)),
    levels = c("Never", "Former", "Current")
  ),
  exposure_primary = rnorm(n),
  bmi = rnorm(n, mean = 27, sd = 4),
  survey_weight = runif(n, min = 0.7, max = 1.4),
  follow_up_years = runif(n, 0.5, 3),
  sample_date_chr = format(
    as.Date("2022-01-01") + sample(0:120, n, replace = TRUE),
    "%d/%m/%Y"
  ),
  binary_1_2 = sample(c(1, 2, -99), n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.24, 0.72, 0.04)),
  binary_1_0 = sample(c(0, 1, -77), n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.68, 0.28, 0.04)),
  continuous_dirty = ifelse(runif(n) < 0.04, -1, rnorm(n, mean = 10, sd = 3))
)

# Binary, continuous, count, and ordinal outcomes
linpred <- -1.1 + 0.55 * dat$exposure_primary + 0.03 * (dat$age_years - 50) +
  0.35 * (dat$sex == "Male") + 0.45 * (dat$smoking_status == "Current") +
  0.25 * (dat$region == "North")
dat$outcome_bin <- rbinom(n, size = 1, prob = plogis(linpred))
dat$outcome_group <- factor(
  dat$outcome_bin,
  levels = c(0, 1),
  labels = c("Negative", "Positive")
)
dat$outcome_cont <- 2 + 0.65 * dat$exposure_primary - 0.2 * (dat$sex == "Male") + rnorm(n)
dat$infections <- rpois(n, dat$follow_up_years * exp(-0.9 + 0.35 * dat$exposure_primary))
dat$severity <- factor(
  sample(c("None", "Mild", "Severe"), n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.60, 0.25, 0.15)),
  levels = c("None", "Mild", "Severe")
)
dat$predicted_flag <- as.integer(dat$exposure_primary + rnorm(n, sd = 0.8) > 0.5)

# Time-to-event outcome with proportional hazards
hazard <- 0.015 * exp(
  0.45 * dat$exposure_primary +
    0.025 * (dat$age_years - 50) +
    0.30 * (dat$sex == "Male") +
    0.40 * (dat$smoking_status == "Current")
)
event_time <- rexp(n, rate = hazard)
censor_time <- runif(n, min = 25, max = 140)
dat$time_days <- pmin(event_time, censor_time)
dat$event <- as.integer(event_time <= censor_time)

# Introduce realistic missingness and variable labels
dat$region[sample(seq_len(n), 15)] <- NA
dat$smoking_status[sample(seq_len(n), 20)] <- NA
attr(dat$exposure_primary, "label") <- "Primary exposure score"

labels <- c(
  age_years = "Age (years)",
  sex = "Sex",
  region = "Region",
  smoking_status = "Smoking status",
  bmi = "Body mass index",
  deprivation = "Deprivation quintile",
  exposure_primary = "Primary exposure score"
)
```

## 2. Data cleaning and missingness helpers

The cleaning functions recode survey-style sentinel values: `binaryCleaner()` maps `1`/`2`
to `1`/`0`, `binaryCleaner_1_0()` preserves `1`/`0` while converting negative sentinel
codes to `NA`, `continuousCleaner()` drops values below a floor, `dateCleaner()` parses dates
while treating REACT missing codes as `NA`, `reactCleaner()` provides a unified wrapper, and
`checkConvertNumeric()` converts numeric-looking character columns to numeric.

```{r cleaning}
cleaned_preview <- data.frame(
  raw_1_2 = dat$binary_1_2[1:6],
  clean_1_2 = binaryCleaner(dat$binary_1_2[1:6]),
  raw_1_0 = dat$binary_1_0[1:6],
  clean_1_0 = binaryCleaner_1_0(dat$binary_1_0[1:6]),
  raw_cont = round(dat$continuous_dirty[1:6], 2),
  clean_cont = round(continuousCleaner(dat$continuous_dirty[1:6], floornumber = 0), 2),
  clean_date = as.character(dateCleaner(dat$sample_date_chr[1:6], dateFormat = "%d/%m/%Y"))
)
knitr::kable(cleaned_preview)

char_df <- data.frame(
  id_code = c("101", "102", NA, "104"),
  category = c("low", "medium", "high", "low"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
str(checkConvertNumeric(char_df))
```

`naReporter()` summarises missing values (`NA`) and IPSOS Mori sentinel missingness codes
(`-91`, `-92`/`-77`, `-99`) across variables in a data frame:

```{r na-reporter}
na_summary <- naReporter(
  dat[, c("age_years", "region", "smoking_status", "binary_1_2", "binary_1_0")]
)
knitr::kable(na_summary)
```

## 3. Cross-tabulations and Table 1

### Cross-tabulation helpers

`crossTab()`, `crossTabContinuous()`, and `crossTabMulti()` build stratified descriptive
summaries, supporting survey weights and optional confidence intervals.

```{r crosstabs}
ct_cat <- crossTab(
  dat = dat,
  rowvar = "smoking_status",
  colvar = "sex",
  include_percentages = TRUE,
  confint = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(ct_cat)

ct_cont <- crossTabContinuous(
  dat = dat,
  rowvar = "bmi",
  colvar = "sex",
  summary_stat = "mean"
)
knitr::kable(ct_cont)
```

### Descriptive Table 1 and display formatting

`tableOne()` summarises continuous and categorical variables overall and by group. With
`statistical_test = TRUE`, tests are chosen automatically (Fisher's exact test when expected
cell counts are $< 5$, otherwise $\chi^2$; $t$-test/ANOVA for means and Wilcoxon/Kruskal-Wallis
for medians) and recorded in `attr(x, "tests")`. Setting `smd = TRUE` adds pairwise
standardised mean differences.

```{r table-one}
table_one <- tableOne(
  dat = dat,
  rowvars = c("age_years", "bmi", "sex", "smoking_status", "region"),
  colvar = "outcome_group",
  cov_names = labels,
  statistical_test = TRUE,
  smd = TRUE
)
knitr::kable(table_one)
attr(table_one, "tests")
```

`tableOneDisplay()` converts a `tableOne()` data frame into a styled `gt` table for HTML or a
`flextable` for Word documents:

```{r table-one-display, eval = requireNamespace("gt", quietly = TRUE)}
tableOneDisplay(table_one, output = "gt", title = "Baseline characteristics by outcome")
```

## 4. Prevalence and stratified tables

`makeTablesNew()` estimates prevalence with Wilson score intervals. By default no assay
correction is applied; supplying `sens` and `spec` applies the Rogan-Gladen correction.
Setting `for_report = TRUE` returns formatted `"Prevalence (95% CI)"` strings.

```{r prevalence}
prevalence <- makeTablesNew(
  dat = dat,
  result_var = "outcome_bin",
  covariates = c("sex", "smoking_status", "region"),
  cov_name_list = labels,
  output_list = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(prevalence)

prevalence_report <- makeTablesNew(
  dat = dat,
  result_var = "outcome_bin",
  covariates = c("sex", "smoking_status"),
  cov_name_list = labels,
  sens = 0.85,
  spec = 0.99,
  for_report = TRUE,
  output_list = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(prevalence_report)
```

`stratifiedTables()` cross-tabulates prevalence across a stratification variable, and
`makeStratifiedPrevalenceTablePlottable()` reshapes the result for `ggplot2`:

```{r stratified-prevalence}
strat_prev <- stratifiedTables(
  dat = dat,
  result_var = "outcome_bin",
  covariates = c("smoking_status", "region"),
  cov_name_list = labels,
  strat_var = "sex",
  include_counts = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(strat_prev)

strat_plot_df <- makeStratifiedPrevalenceTablePlottable(strat_prev)
knitr::kable(head(strat_plot_df, 6), digits = 2)
```

## 5. Single-model effect tables

For an individual fitted model (`glm`, `lm`, `coxph`, etc.), `makeORTable()`, `makeRDTable()`,
and `makeRRTable()` extract formatted odds/hazard ratios, marginal risk differences, and
marginal risk ratios:

```{r single-model}
fit_glm <- glm(
  outcome_bin ~ exposure_primary + smoking_status + age_years + sex,
  family = binomial(),
  data = dat
)

knitr::kable(makeORTable(fit_glm, dp = 2))
knitr::kable(makeRDTable(fit_glm, variable_name = "smoking_status", data = dat, n_sim = 50, dp = 3))
knitr::kable(makeRRTable(fit_glm, variable_name = "smoking_status", data = dat, n_sim = 50, dp = 2))
```

## 6. Sequential and batch regression models

### Binary outcomes: Odds Ratios, marginal Risk Differences, and marginal Risk Ratios

`ModelMakerMultiRD()` fits each variable of interest across sequential adjustment stages.
For binary outcomes it computes odds ratios (`df_output`), marginal risk differences
(`df_output_RDs` when `include_rd = TRUE`), marginal risk ratios (`df_output_RRs` when
`include_rr = TRUE`), and Benjamini-Hochberg $q$-values (`Q_value`) within each adjustment stage.

```{r models-binary}
models <- ModelMakerMultiRD(
  dat = dat,
  list_of_variables_of_interest = c("exposure_primary", "smoking_status", "bmi"),
  outcome = "outcome_bin",
  joint_adjustment_vars = c("age_years", "sex", "region"),
  cov_name_list = labels,
  include_rd = TRUE,
  include_rr = TRUE,
  n_sim = 50,
  ncores = 1
)
knitr::kable(models$df_output)
knitr::kable(
  head(models$plot_output[, c(
    "Variable", "Category", "adjustment_label",
    "OR", "Lower", "Upper", "P_value", "Q_value"
  )]),
  digits = 3
)
```

### Alternative GLM families: Modified Poisson, Poisson rates, and Ordinal/Multinomial

The `family` argument selects alternative regression models:

- `family = "modified_poisson"`: Poisson regression with robust (HC0 sandwich) standard errors for direct risk ratio (`RR`) estimation.
- `family = "poisson"` with `offset`: incidence rate ratios (`IRR`).
- `family = "ordinal"` or `"multinomial"` (or automatic detection on multi-level factor outcomes).

```{r models-families}
mod_poisson <- ModelMakerMultiRD(
  dat = dat,
  list_of_variables_of_interest = c("exposure_primary", "smoking_status"),
  outcome = "outcome_bin",
  joint_adjustment_vars = c("age_years", "sex"),
  cov_name_list = labels,
  family = "modified_poisson",
  ncores = 1
)
knitr::kable(mod_poisson$df_output)

rates <- ModelMakerMultiRD(
  dat = dat,
  list_of_variables_of_interest = "exposure_primary",
  outcome = "infections",
  joint_adjustment_vars = c("age_years", "sex"),
  cov_name_list = labels,
  family = "poisson",
  offset = "follow_up_years",
  ncores = 1
)
knitr::kable(rates$df_output)

severity_mod <- ModelMakerMultiRD(
  dat = dat,
  list_of_variables_of_interest = "smoking_status",
  outcome = "severity",
  joint_adjustment_vars = "age_years",
  cov_name_list = labels,
  ncores = 1
)
knitr::kable(severity_mod$df_output)
```

### Cox proportional-hazards models

Supplying `time` (with `family = "cox"` or `family = "auto"`) fits Cox proportional-hazards
models via `survival::coxph()`. Outputs are labelled as hazard ratios (`HR`), `plot_output`
records level-specific `events`, and `diagnostics` includes per-term and global Schoenfeld
residual proportional-hazards test $p$-values (`ph_p_value` and `ph_global_p_value`).

```{r models-cox}
cox_models <- ModelMakerMultiRD(
  dat = dat,
  list_of_variables_of_interest = c("exposure_primary", "smoking_status", "sex"),
  outcome = "event",
  time = "time_days",
  joint_adjustment_vars = c("age_years", "region"),
  cov_name_list = labels,
  ncores = 1
)
knitr::kable(cox_models$df_output)
knitr::kable(
  cox_models$diagnostics[, c(
    "Variable", "stage", "adjusted_vars", "nobs", "events",
    "ph_p_value", "ph_global_p_value"
  )],
  digits = 3
)
```

## 7. Publication-ready regression tables with `modelOutputDisplay()`

`modelOutputDisplay()` formats the output of `ModelMakerMultiRD()`, `ModelMakerMulti()`,
`modelMakerSequentialRD()`, or `run_auto_tableone_regressions()` into a clean display table.
It can return a `flextable` (for Word), a `gt` table (for HTML), or a formatted `data.frame`
(via `output = "data.frame"`).

You can choose which adjustment stages to show (`stages = "crude_and_full"`, `"all"`, or
`"full"`), relabel stages via `stage_labels`, and append marginal risk differences
(`include_rd = TRUE`), marginal risk ratios (`include_rr = TRUE`), $p$-values
(`include_p = TRUE`), or Benjamini-Hochberg $q$-values (`include_q = TRUE`).

```{r model-output-display-df}
reg_table_df <- modelOutputDisplay(
  models,
  output = "data.frame",
  stages = "crude_and_full",
  stage_labels = c(
    crude = "Unadjusted",
    `adj_age_years+sex+region` = "Fully adjusted"
  ),
  include_rd = TRUE,
  include_rr = TRUE,
  include_p = TRUE,
  include_q = TRUE
)
knitr::kable(reg_table_df)
```

For Cox models, `modelOutputDisplay()` automatically includes an `Events` column when
`include_events = TRUE` (the default):

```{r model-output-display-cox}
cox_table_df <- modelOutputDisplay(
  cox_models,
  output = "data.frame",
  stages = "crude_and_full",
  stage_labels = c(
    crude = "Unadjusted",
    `adj_age_years+region` = "Adjusted for age & region"
  ),
  include_events = TRUE,
  include_p = TRUE
)
knitr::kable(cox_table_df)
```

When `gt` or `flextable` is installed, pass `output = "gt"` or `output = "flextable"` for
styled HTML or Word tables with grouped adjustment-stage spanners:

```{r model-output-display-gt, eval = requireNamespace("gt", quietly = TRUE)}
modelOutputDisplay(
  models,
  output = "gt",
  stages = "crude_and_full",
  include_rd = TRUE,
  title = "Crude and adjusted associations with outcome"
)
```

## 8. Forest plots and collinearity diagnostics

### Forest plots across effect scales

`plotReactForest()` accepts batch model outputs, tidy plotting data frames, single fitted
models, or named lists of fitted models. Setting `show_estimates = TRUE` adds a right-hand
table column printing the formatted estimate, confidence interval, $p$-value, and sample size.

```{r forest-or}
plotReactForest(
  models,
  adjustment_numbers = c(0, 3),
  adjustment_descriptions = c("Crude", "Adjusted for age, sex and region"),
  show_estimates = TRUE,
  title = "Odds ratios for binary outcome"
)
```

Plot marginal risk differences (`effect = "RD"`) or hazard ratios from Cox models
(`effect = "HR"`):

```{r forest-rd-hr}
plotReactForest(
  models,
  effect = "RD",
  adjustment_numbers = c(0, 3),
  adjustment_descriptions = c("Crude", "Adjusted"),
  title = "Marginal risk differences"
)

plotReactForest(
  cox_models,
  effect = "HR",
  adjustment_numbers = c(0, 2),
  adjustment_descriptions = c("Crude", "Adjusted for age and region"),
  show_estimates = TRUE,
  title = "Cox proportional-hazards models"
)
```

Fitted models can also be compared directly by passing a named list:

```{r forest-models}
model_list <- list(
  Crude = glm(outcome_bin ~ exposure_primary + smoking_status, binomial, dat),
  Adjusted = glm(outcome_bin ~ exposure_primary + smoking_status + age_years + sex, binomial, dat)
)
plotReactForest(model_list, variables = c("exposure_primary", "smoking_status"))
```

### Variance inflation factor (VIF) trajectories

`plotReactVIF()` visualises how variance inflation factors evolve across sequential adjustment
stages to help diagnose multicollinearity:

```{r plot-vif}
vif_df <- data.frame(
  Variable = rep(c("Primary exposure score", "Body mass index"), each = 4),
  adjustment = rep(0:3, times = 2),
  vif = c(1.00, 1.08, 1.15, 1.24, 1.00, 1.12, 1.35, 1.62)
)
plotReactVIF(
  vif_df,
  adjustment_numbers = 0:3,
  adjustment_descriptions = c("Crude", "+ Age", "+ Sex", "+ Region")
)
```

## 9. Automated analysis and narrative report

`run_auto_tableone_regressions()` combines `tableOne()`, sequential regression modelling,
diagnostics, and an automated markdown narrative ranking predictors by their most-adjusted
association. Its output can also be passed directly to `modelOutputDisplay()`.

```{r auto-report, results = "asis"}
auto <- run_auto_tableone_regressions(
  dat = dat,
  outcome = "outcome_bin",
  covariates = c("age_years", "sex"),
  independent_variables = c("exposure_primary", "smoking_status", "bmi", "age_years"),
  cov_names = labels,
  include_rd = TRUE,
  n_sim = 30,
  ncores = 1
)
cat(auto$report_markdown)
```

```{r auto-display}
knitr::kable(modelOutputDisplay(auto, output = "data.frame", stages = "crude_and_full"))
```

## 10. Epidemiological and formatting utilities

`calculateEpiStats()` computes classification performance metrics (accuracy, sensitivity,
specificity, PPV, NPV, $F_1$, Matthew's correlation coefficient, likelihood ratios, and AUC)
with exact binomial confidence intervals. `specifyDecimal()`, `pValEpiConverter()`, and
`pvalAsterisker()` format numbers and $p$-values for tables and text.

```{r epi-stats}
epi_stats <- calculateEpiStats(
  prediction = dat$predicted_flag,
  outcome = dat$outcome_bin,
  returnAllStats = TRUE
)
knitr::kable(epi_stats, digits = 3)

p_demo <- c(0.42, 0.038, 0.004, 0.00002)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  raw_p = p_demo,
  epi_format = pValEpiConverter(p_demo),
  asterisks = pvalAsterisker(p_demo, return_p = TRUE),
  decimal_3sf = specifyDecimal(c(pi, exp(1), 0.0456, 12.3), k = 3)
))
```

## 11. Themes, Imperial palettes, and export helpers

`theme_react()` and `theme_mw()` pair with `scale_fill_imperial()` and `scale_color_imperial()`
(powered by `imperial_palettes`):

```{r themes}
p_box <- ggplot(dat, aes(x = sex, y = exposure_primary, fill = sex)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_imperial(palette = "cool") +
  theme_react() +
  labs(title = "theme_react() with Imperial 'cool' palette", x = NULL, y = "Primary exposure score")
p_box

ggplot(dat, aes(x = age_years, y = outcome_cont, colour = smoking_status)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.45) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_color_imperial(palette = "default") +
  theme_mw() +
  labs(title = "theme_mw() with Imperial 'default' palette", x = "Age (years)", y = "Continuous outcome")
```

`saveREACTtable()`, `saveREACTplot()`, `saveREACT()`, and `savePrettyExcelWorkbook()` write
formatted outputs to disk:

```{r export}
out_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "overreact-vignette")
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

saveREACTtable(prevalence, outpath = out_dir, filename = "prevalence")
saveREACTplot(p_box, figpath = out_dir, filename = "exposure_boxplot", width = 6, height = 4, savePDF = FALSE)
if (requireNamespace("openxlsx", quietly = TRUE)) {
  savePrettyExcelWorkbook(
    list(`Table 1` = table_one, Prevalence = prevalence, Regression = reg_table_df),
    workbookName = "tables",
    outpath = out_dir
  )
}
sort(list.files(out_dir))
```
